challenge.better_approach: Considered having the cairn hook recompile and commit the commons itself: a hook writing a second repo is a writer nobody owns, and it would commit commons content the lander never saw. Considered a verify_lab call over the whole lab: that reds every commit while any unrelated copy drifts, so the tooth judges only the charters this commit stages.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the commons beside is <repo>/../CairnCommons on every box and worktree, as the compiler's _default_roots assumes. A checkout with no commons beside can no longer commit a charter; the refusal says so. Hollow and scratch worktrees under /tmp commit no charters (they run proofs), so they are untouched.
challenge.prior_art: cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/compiler.py verify_lab compares source to lab copy over the working tree; this reads the index and commons HEAD instead, reusing lab_filename and gather_sources for the name. Nothing in the tester or artifact hooks reads the commons today.
challenge.real_collision: A distinction with 'commit often': only a charter change is held, and only until its twin lands, which the lander already must do for the lab to be true. The order commons-first is the orchestrator's ruling, so no Akien question.

answers.falsifier: In a scratch cairn beside a scratch commons, a commit or land staging a charter with no twin at commons HEAD leaves HEAD unmoved and names 'land the commons lab copy <name> first'; red on A1's build, where it commits. Horizon: the next charter land on main finds its twin already in the commons.
answers.how: A tester module cairn/devices/tester/lab_twin.py reads git diff --cached for intention+why.json paths (A, M, D; renames split). For each add or modify it names the lab copy with cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/compiler.py's lab_filename over gather_sources, reads the staged bytes (git show :path) and the commons twin at <repo>/../CairnCommons HEAD (git show HEAD:intentions-congruency-lab/<name>), and refuses when the twin is missing or differs. A deleted charter is refused while its copy still stands at commons HEAD. Charters gather_sources skips (proofs/, validations/, dot dirs) need no twin. No commons beside refuses, named. Each refusal line ends 'land the commons lab copy <name> first'. cairn/devices/tester/hooks/pre-commit runs it, blocking, after the first artifact check; a land reaches it through pre-merge-commit (db250e9bf3f9). The proof cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_charter_lands_after_its_lab_twin.py builds a scratch cairn and a scratch CairnCommons side by side, with the real hooks installed by install_hook, the real module and compiler, and A1's passing stub doors, and commits and merges for real.
answers.traces_to: Law 4 and Law 5: the thing and the story of the thing may live in two roots but may never contradict each other, and a rule that matters is enforced by the commit door, not by remembering to recompile.
answers.what: The commit door refuses a cairn commit or land that changes an intention+why.json until the commons beside holds its lab copy, byte for byte, at its HEAD.

bullets.text: 77 of 304 charter writes since 10-16 left the lab stale; the commit door now holds a charter until its twin lands in the commons.

title: The commit door refuses a cairn commit or land that changes an intention+why.json until the commons beside holds its lab
